I loved this game, such a mood, it's not very long but the level of detail in each of the game's areas is completely insane, I took many pauses just to take in the environment.

I've been waiting for what feels like a decade for this game, ever since I saw the first gifs of the concept for that "HK Game" on the web, I must say that the final product lives up to my expectations.

I adored this game! It was perfect adventure game and just enjoyed the exploration and being a cat!

I do wish it was longer though, but we shall see if there maybe more!

Stray is a masterpiece of video game narrative. Nothing else even comes close. The story is brutal, challenging, bold, and almost never "fun". It is harrowing, forcing the player to confront cats in a way video games never do

In a medium where everything is John Wick, Stray is Schindler's List. And just like that film, there were times when I wasn't sure I could keep going. It is a relentless emotional assault that I suspect will force even the most jaded gamer to feel empathy

The game is a work of art - every aspect feels crafted at the highest level. Visuals, audio, controls, animation, level design, performance. It is astounding. And frequently beautiful. With moments you NEVER find in video games. But I cannot overstate how harrowing it is.

It feels like 2 seasons of the darkest TV show you'll ever find, and it frequently better than most TV on the air. That's saying a lot. I think it is an IMPORTANT game. It tore me up, and I will never, ever forget it. Stray is a game that will change you.

In short, Stray put me through hell. I did not enjoy it. I wasn't supposed to. I was affected by it. Like no game before. I am in awe of it. I am recovering from it.
One of the best storyline, beautiful environment, and high graphics game I've ever played. I shed a tear at the end

I've never written any kind of review on steam before, nor a positive or negative one. This game made do it for once. I'm no game reviewer, so just from a casual point of view, the game is beautiful looking, the controls are excellent, the story is compelling, and overall the general experience was great, and for someone close to cats, touching in a way.

I'm writting this review not only because the game deserves it, but to add one more to the thousands of other positive ones, and hopefully make the team consider working on a sequel.

i thought this was going to be a cute game about cats and robots.

it was. but it was also so much more. from the fun side quests, to freaky undertones, to terrifying enemies, to an emotional story line... the list could go on.

i heavily recommend Stray to anyone who wants a little bit of everything out of a game. especially a dedicated meow button :)

Both the end, and beginning gave me a real gut punch... But every second was worth it! The story was movie level, each interaction was thoughtful and (/s)way to real. And using motion capture on actual cats for your animations? incredible!
( Spoilers!! )

During the ending, the fact it was "open to interpretation" whether or not you reunited with your family was honestly the most painful and sad any story, game or movie, has ever made me experience. So I looked long and far for some answer, and laned on this wonderful piece of information.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tEOEczZQHbo&t=142s

Now, while its still "open to interpretation", This is how I chose to interpret it (And it seems the rest of the community does as well).

This game is far more intense than I ever would have expected or anticipated. I was expecting a good game based on story alone, but the intensity makes it a great game! Do buy it, especially if you can grab it during a sale.
It's a game about a cat interacting with robots and it shows more humanity than the last 10 AAA releases combined. Beautiful, poetic, just downright wonderful.
While a little short, the game is super refreshing, interesting and overall just beautiful. If you know a way of wiping my memory so I can play the game again, please do let me know
short fun game, the way things used to be (and should be (I hate 140 hour behemoths (unless it is bg3)))

Got this game yesterday and I've been playing for 5+ hours!!
It's a really cute game with cool world, lots of space to explore, great music track and ofcourse, our cute protagonist cat.
The difficulty level is easy to medium

For a protagonist given no dialog whatsoever (well, other than "meow") this game still manages to tell a profoundly moving story. The world is gorgeously detailed, it's neither a fast-paced stress-inducer nor a boring snoozefest - the pace is exactly what you make it to be at any point in the game. The opening chapter is an incredibly intuitive tutorial, and whoever worked on the cat animations and behavior did their homework to almost OCD levels of thorough. The camera angles are perfect for showing the world through the cat's eyes, and the immersiveness is stunning. And they managed to solidly project a personality from every robot, which couldn't have been easy. Highly recommended, worth every penny.

PS: I keep hearing people say it's "about 4-6 hours of content"...I dunno where that number comes from. Exploring everywhere and taking in all the details of the setting, solving the puzzles, finding the hints and all the memories, uncovering all of the story, and doing so at a comfortable pace took me about 12 hours. 10/10 would adopt the cat, too.

At first, I wondered why people liked such a simple and silly game; I played it for an hour or two and then dropped it. However, about a year later, I decided to return to it with the goal of unlocking all the Steam achievements. That’s when I discovered a masterpiece I would never forget. Thanks for the enjoyable experience—100% complete.

Nothing about this game is ground breaking.......But anyone saying this is a bad game is a complete fool looking for attention. The game has an excellent level of presentation and simple but fun game play. Very short but has nicely thought out storytelling with excellent aesthetics making this a pleasure to go through. Worth playing through for sure!!! Unless you are one of those pple determined to make sure everyone thinks it is poop.

PROS: Runs smoothly, jumping is satisfactory (you don't have to worry about balance because you are a cat and not a puny human with a controller), atmosphere is desolate but still hopeful. There's a dedicated "meow" button and you can knock things off surfaces like the lil jerk you are. Nice soundtrack, adorable robots.

CONS: There is some scratching mechanics but I've so far seen a bunch of couches and couldn't destroy any of those. As a cat owner, I feel like I could have had the opportunity to finally understand what's so great about shredding furniture. Also cats are vicious killing machines but I can only shake off the buggers that come after me instead of attacking them.

(I will update this review in the future)

SO good!! The vibes are everything, and the story is overall amazing.

It's just a cat, but this game REALLY used an animal to it's full potential for such an amazing story line!! I couldn't imagine ANY better cat game like this one being created.

The game is also filled of interactive challenges, not just the amazing heartwarming storyline. Personally, I love story games and interactive games, so this is definitely a must play for me. The animations are also servery good.

Overall, this game is just a masterpiece. It's definetely worth buying, anybody who says otherwise is so wrong. It hurts to see how underrated it is!!

Stray is a purr-fect masterpiece that seamlessly weaves together a beautifully crafted world, stunning art style, meticulous detail, and a captivating narrative. The cityscape is visually enchanting, filled with cozy hideaways and unexpected surprises. The game's attention to detail is astounding, from rain-soaked streets to the bustling life of stray animals.

Stray's gameplay is both intuitive and engaging, allowing you to gracefully navigate the city, solve puzzles, and interact with the environment. The feline perspective adds a unique charm, capturing the essence of a cat's curiosity. The narrative is heartwarming and mysterious, with memorable characters contributing to the overall allure.

As the credits rolled, the anticipation for the sequel was palpable. Stray is not just a game; it's a fun and unforgettable experience that will leave you eagerly awaiting the next adventure in this remarkable world.

I absolutely loved the game.
Ever since I first saw the trailer, I knew I had to play it and when I did, I was not disappointed.

The storytelling, the characters, the environment, simply the atmosphere are all exceptionally well done. For everyone who wants to relax, do small sidequests, get some collectibles and have a bit of action from time to time: this is it. Especially for all the animal lovers out there.

The game is more so on the "shorter" side game-time wise. I'd say 6 - 10 hours, depending on how much you collect, talk to NPCs, etc.

Overall, this is a total win/win for everyone who simply wants to enjoy.
Beautiful game and excellent for the steam deck! The game does not take long to beat, but has gorgeous graphics, a great soundstage, engaging storyline, and a very cute cat.

I got baited by the Overwhelmingly Positive rating. It's one of these games which has easy but cute gameplay mechanics and cool graphics and basically that’s all. Scratching the rug, knocking things off the shelves and looking at cool views gets old after a few hours. Games like this usually have to offer a great plot and background to keep involved. I finished it only because I was hoping for some cool plot twist or explanation of what happened and what I got was some scraps of information which didn’t even make a consistent story. Some things just weren’t explained and also cause and effect was not clear. I even searched for more information thinking that I skipped something. The ending was disappointing since the outside world wasn’t shown as well as any hint as to what happens next. But I appreciate the auto camera which didn’t trigger my motion sickness.
Any game you get to play as a cat is a great game. Cats are awesome.

It has beautiful art style along with a great soundtrack. The animation is top tier and what else could be better than playing as a cat. The story line is great with really good puzzle type missions and very cool semi-open world approach.
This game is so cozy and kinda silly its fun puzzles are really good and is just really good love it i really reccomend if u like cats.

Stray is a game where you play as a cat that trapped in an underground metropolis full with intelligent robots and parasites that can eat everything is a good game.

The story of the game is rich and has good storytelling ranging from wholesome to emotional. It's a good game for someone who loves cats, robots, sci-fi and good and yet rich story. The lore of the game is interesting and cool how the humans has gone extinct due the virus and transfer their minds to the robots, which the parasites can still eat the metal parts of the robot. I really like this concept. 

I do like how you can play as a cat in a third person view or should I say third cat view get it? I do like how it lets you to automatically jump instead of accidentallly falling down the ground. I do like how you can nuzzles legs of the robots like a cat.
Lovely game! Gorgeous visuals, adorable and touching story. I really liked the soundtrack! Has a vibe similar to the Portal series. If you liked that, you'll like this too!

One of the best storyline game I have played thus far. It conjured the small, subtle details and crafted an incredibly emotional gameplay. 
The gameplay itself is very fun and relaxing. The behaviors of cats were captured perfectly through the protagonists and its family. 
You only have to download 5-6 gigabytes to receive an extremely detailed and atmospheric gameplay. Definitely a huge win. 

Feedback (spoilers):
I would say though, I had hoped the protagonist to reunite with its family but that does not seem to be the case. A tad bit sad but it is realistic in that sense. 
Furthermore, it would be great to be able to explore the outside world with how it has been hyped up all game through pictures and paintings. A DLC expansion after the ending for this specific topic would be very much welcomed. 

Final Ratings:
Easily top tier, single-player story game of all time. That is my opinion, it's GOATED.

As a professional cat myself the game play mechanics come naturally to me. So far the story is that i've fallen and trapped myself far away from my fellow felines and must return, a very cat thing to do. The game play is as to be expected, if you need help meow. Some of the jumps can be tricky to get the prompt to show and you must look a very certain way. If you're stuck just keep exploring the area or look for an item that can help.

2 Paws way up

A Cozy, Emotional Cat Adventure Through a Lonely Future.

Stray is the first game I’ve ever played where the protagonist is a cat — and that alone makes it feel special. At the beginning, I thought I’d be interacting more with other cats, but that only lasts a short while before you fall into a dark, gloomy underground city with no humans — only machines. A glimpse at a possible future?

The story revolves around the cat finding a way back to the outside world, with small side quests where you help different robots along the journey. The visuals are beautiful and the atmosphere really pulls you in. The music is nice too, and the game mostly feels calm and chill… until the Zurks start chasing you and you’re suddenly sprinting for your life.

The adventure is pretty short though — I wish the story lasted longer and maybe introduced more cats later in the game. Still, it’s a relaxing and emotional experience, especially with B-12 by your side. The ending hits hard when B-12 sacrifices himself so the cat can escape to freedom.

If you want a unique, cozy puzzle-adventure where you get to explore like a curious cat, Stray is absolutely worth playing.
